lectures.title: Rendering Content Correctly on the Server

cues.en: The problem in our application here simply is that because I'm populating my store with the preloaded
data and I'm not using the preloaded data directly in my Dom in my markup, actually, when Svelte renders
this page for the first time, it doesn't have any meetups on there.
It just has the data in the store, which will eventually, like a millisecond later populate the Dom,
but it's not rendering it on the server.
It's not rendering the dom on the server yet.
To work around that, we can simply overwrite our fetched meetups instead of the loaded meetups here
with the store data.
Now what do we mean with that?
These are the meetups we're getting from the server side preloading.
And then here in on Mount, I'm setting up a subscription.
To override my loaded meetups, which is the variable I just deleted.
And then I set my meetups in the store to the fetched meetups I got.
And actually we can first set our store meetups to the fetch meetups and then set up a subscription
where I set fetch meetups to the meetups store, which of course are the meetups I already got.
The advantage now just is that I have my store and my fetched meetups here in sync and now all the places
on the page where we refer to loaded meetups in the markup and in the script file up there, we now
use fetched meetups again.
The advantage of this approach is if I run NPM run dev real quick that it should still work as before,
but now it actually finishes the creation of the page on the server.
It creates the full markup on the page.
So if I reload this page we get the same as before.
But now you also don't see that animate in thing.
The animation is missing because we're really getting the finished markup.
That's the difference.
And the advantage is that if I now export this again, since it has the full markup, it automatically
checks all the links it finds.
And we do have links to our dynamic routes and therefore, since it finds links, it is able to create
them and hence you now find these folders with their own HTML files for our dynamic routes.
So Sapper is able of doing that.
You just have to make sure that you really return your finished markup and you don't render the markup
on the client.
Now with that, we have another static app here in the export folder.
And what you could do now is take the entire content here, all the files in the export folder and again
put them on a static host like AWS S3 or Firebase hosting.
So the content here goes onto a static host in your normal svelte app.
The content here goes into a static host, and the only thing that needs a nodejs server is the content
in the build folder.
This would have to be deployed onto a server that is capable of running JS.
